renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Too much love gives you a mind — a mind gone off wanting, and her power, Śaṅkara's own: picture her always, then Śiva. Picture the open in the things inside you and in all things — sit with her open even there: even knowing turns calm.

Remember being clean just a little — then hear Śambhu's view: neither clean nor unclean — thought-free, and you may be happy. The Bhairava-state is everywhere, even in plain everyday things — nothing past it: going not-two.
Hold foe and friend the same, praise and blame the same — brahma's fullness known: you may be happy. Picture neither hate anywhere nor love — free of both, brahman slides into the middle.

The unknowable, the ungraspable, the open, the gone-from-being — picture all of it as Bhairava: at that end, waking rises. Lasting, propless, open, everywhere, uncounted — set the mind in the outer sky: walked into the skyless.

Wherever the mind runs — that, that, by that, right then — leave no-standing behind: then waveless you may be. Fear rings through all, the all-giving whole that holds everything — say the Bhairava-word over and over: Śiva.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Excess devotion mints a mind — unhooked mind, her power, his power: run her always, then Śiva. Open in the inside things, open in all things — her, meditated even there: even knowing chills out.
Flash of remembered clean — then Śambhu's take: neither clean nor dirty — blank and allowed to be happy. Bhairava-state everyplace, even the regular stuff — no beyond: nondual locomotion.
Enemy equals friend, flowers equal insults — brahma's fullness clocked: happiness unlocked. Nowhere hate, nowhere heat — clear of both and brahman cruises down the middle.

Unknowable, ungrabbable, open, off-the-map-of-being — all of it Bhairava: waking rises at that end. Permanent, propless, open, omnipresent, uncountable — mind in the outer sky, walked into the skyless.
Mind anywhere — that, that, thereby, right then — drop the standing habit: waveless mode, permitted. Fear ringing through everything, the giver-whole holding it all — Bhairava-word on loop: Śiva.
